subject: Retention origins: why streaming snippets and session state sometimes persist
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@brightbank.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: 2029-06-01T09:14:00Z
Subject: Quick clarification: why are some streaming snippets showing up in audit logs?

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two follow-ups from the security team: when we use the hosted API with streaming enabled, we sometimes see short snippets in our access/audit exports that look like partial generated text. We need to understand: are those streaming fragments treated as "request" (customer input) or "output" (model generated), and do they follow the same default retention window?

Specifically:
- Will streaming partial outputs be retained beyond the session TTL by default?
- Where are those fragments stored (EU-only storage vs transient memory)?
- If we request an account-wide shorter retention (e.g., 7 days), does that affect streaming snippets or only finalized outputs?

I've attached our questionnaire for your security review. Can you confirm the default behaviour and point us to the deletion/runbook?

Best,
Elena Ramos
Head of Security Operations
BrightBank

Attachment: BrightBank_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: 2029-06-01T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: why are some streaming snippets showing up in audit logs?

Hi Elena —

Really useful questions, thanks for sending the questionnaire. Looping in Kim from Product (cc) and Naomi from Security so we can give a concise, authoritative answer. I'll summarize the short answers here and Kim/Naomi can expand:

- Short answer: streaming fragments are generated outputs by the model; they are not treated as new customer inputs.
- Default retention: hosted requests/outputs are retained per our default telemetry window (45 days) unless the customer configures a shorter policy or requests erasure.
- Residency: data for EU customers is stored in EU-region stores by default.

Kim/Naomi — can you confirm and add any exceptions (KV cache, crash dumps, diagnostic traces) and link the runbook? We should also confirm what changes with an account-level retention override.

Thanks,
Dylan
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2029-06-02T08:27:00Z
Subject: Internal: detailed retention breakdown for Elena / BrightBank

Dylan — short technical breakdown that you can paste into the customer reply. Naomi, please flag anything I miss.

Definitions (how we categorize items by default):
- "Request / Prompt": the text payload the customer sends to the API (user prompt, system messages). These are considered customer inputs and are captured in the request log. Default retention: 45 days on hosted accounts unless overridden.
- "Model Output (finalized)": the completed generated text after the response completes. Treated as an output artifact; default retention: 45 days.
- "Streaming fragments / partial outputs": transient tokens emitted during a streaming response. Behavioral notes:
  - We consider streaming fragments to be part of the model output stream, not additional customer inputs.
  - By default, streaming fragments are not written to the long-term archival store unless one of the following occurs: the response errors mid-stream and a diagnostic trace is captured; the request triggers our telemetry sampling; or the customer enables audit-log persistence for full transcripts.
  - Transient state (KV cache / prefix cache) lives on the serving node and is evicted per session lifetime; it is not copied to the archival telemetry store unless captured for diagnostics.
- "Derived artifacts" (embeddings, vectors, reranks): persisted according to the customer's storage settings (often longer than the 45-day telemetry window if the customer stores them in their account).

Residency: for EU tenants we store archived request/response logs in EU-region object storage. Short-lived caches and runtime memory always live in the region where the request was served.

Account-level overrides: when a customer asks for a shorter default (e.g., 7 days), we apply the new TTL to archived request/response logs and to scheduled purge jobs. This override does not change in-memory caches or kernel-level KV eviction timing — those are session-local and evict immediately per runtime policy.

Deletion / Erasure workflow (summary):
- Automatic TTL: scheduled job removes archived records once TTL expires (configurable per account).
- Customer-initiated erase: submit a support request (link below) -> Support triggers an account erasure job for hosted archives -> audit logs and backups are included per our runbook and retention exceptions.
- Emergency erase (legal/compliance): handled via our expedited runbook with engineering involvement.

Exceptions to note:
- Diagnostic traces: if a request caused a crash or is sampled for debugging, we may capture additional context that can include streaming fragments; those traces are tagged and have separate retention decisions (can be excluded via SOC/compliance config).
- Marketplace / third-party integrations: if a customer exports transcripts to an external sink (S3, BigQuery), Redwood cannot delete those targets — we flag that prominently during procurement.

Links / artifacts to share with Elena:
- Retention runbook (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/s/retention-runbook
- Public KB (customer-facing): https://docs.redwood.ai/retention#hosted-defaults

If that looks good, Dylan, send to Elena with the two bullets at top for clarity + the runbook link and our suggested proposal: propose a 7-day trial TTL for BrightBank, run for 30 days, then decide.

—Kim
VP, Product (Redwood Inference)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@brightbank.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2029-06-03T14:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick clarification: why are some streaming snippets showing up in audit logs?

Hi Elena —

Thanks for the detailed questions and the questionnaire. Quick summary up front, then details and next steps:

Summary (short answers)
- Streaming fragments are considered part of the model output stream, not new customer inputs.
- Default archived retention for requests and outputs on hosted accounts is 45 days; streaming fragments are not persisted to archival storage by default unless sampled, instrumented for diagnostics, or explicitly configured for transcript persistence.
- EU customers have archived logs stored in EU-region object stores by default.
- You can request an account-level TTL override (we can set 7 days); that applies to archived logs — it does not accelerate in-memory eviction (which is immediate per session).

Details (expanded)
- What we keep by default: both prompt (request) and finalized model output are written to the hosted telemetry archives and subject to the account TTL (45 days default).
- Streaming fragments: normally streamed to the client and held in ephemeral runtime memory; only written to archive if one of these happens: an error/trace capture, telemetry sampling, or explicit transcript/audit persist enabled by the customer.
- KV cache/prefix cache: ephemeral to the serving node; evicted at session end or per cache policy; not copied to long-term storage.
- Derivatives (embeddings, reranks): persist per customer storage settings and may have different retention.

Deletion / Erasure path
- Automatic TTL purge runs daily and removes archived entries older than the configured TTL.
- For full account erasure, file a support request; we run the erasure job and return a verification report.
- For expedited legal requests, we follow our expedited runbook with engineering and compliance oversight.

Next steps we recommend
1) If BrightBank wants to trial a 7-day archived TTL, we can enable that for a 30-day pilot and provide monitoring logs so you can verify tokens are removed as expected.
2) We'll attach the customer-facing KB and our internal runbook for your security team to review.
3) Naomi can set a short call to talk through sampling/diagnostic exceptions if you want those turned off.

Links and artifacts attached: BrightBank_Security_Questionnaire_v2.xlsx (your file), redwood-retention-flowchart.png, retention runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/s/retention-runbook

Let me know if you want me to schedule the pilot change to 7 days and Naomi will lead the verification.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
